title: The hard bars first
summary: Find the two hardest bars of your piece and practise those first, before anything else.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil

figure.alt: A row of eight boxes, one for each bar of the piece. The third and sixth are shaded, standing for the two hard bars you find first and practise before playing the piece through.

steps.title: The hard bars first
steps.body:
Most practice goes like this: play the piece from the start, hit the hard bit, stumble, start again. The easy bars get played twenty times. The hard bars get played twice, badly. So the easy bars get better and the hard bars stay hard.

This week you turn that around. The hard bars come first.

1. Play the piece once through, slowly, and mark the two bars where you stumble. A pencil circle on the page is enough.
2. Practise only those bars, five times each, slowly enough that nothing goes wrong.
3. Now play the piece once through. Notice what the hard bars feel like now.

Do this four times this week, about 15 minutes each. Four short sittings teach your fingers more than one long one, because the sleep in between is when fingers keep what they learned.

At the end of the week, record the piece once through and write the Practice log.

figure.alt: A row of eight boxes for the piece's bars, the third and sixth shaded. Each sitting starts with those two hard bars, five slow times each, before the piece is played once through.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: circle the two hard bars, five slow times each, then once through
Sitting 2: the two hard bars five times each, then once through
Sitting 3: the two hard bars five times each, then once through
Sitting 4: the two hard bars five times each, then once through as if recording
One piece you already know, played once, for fun

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Say the name of the piece, then play it once through, hands in the frame. Slips stay in. This is the week 1 version, and it is supposed to sound like week 1.

extras.title: Four bars of your own
extras.body:
Make up four bars of your own on the keys.

Start with a question: what would a piece about rain sound like?

Three constraints: use only five notes, keep one steady beat, and end on the note you started on.

Sketch first: write the note names on paper before you play them.

You know it works when someone else can hum it back after hearing it twice.
